newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold makes foray into S. America with Brazil deal.
newsitem.headline: Ahold makes foray into S. America with Brazil deal.

text.p: AMSTERDAM, Netherlands - Dutch food retailer Ahold NV underlined its global ambitions on Monday by announcing plans to take 50 percent of Brazilian supermarket chain Bompreco, its first foray into South America.

Ahold has annual sales of about $24 billion in the United States, the Netherlands and other European countries. Bompreco is Brazil's fourth largest food retailer and market leader in the country's northeast with annual sales of some $1.4 billion.

Earlier this year, Ahold roughly doubled its turnover in the United States by acquiring the Massachusetts-based supermarket chain Stop & Shop. It has also recently expanded into Asia where it has set up joint ventures in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and China.
Though most analysts were upbeat about the Brazil deal, some worried it would expose Ahold to the consumer credit business.
Bompreco runs a customer loyalty programme, offering customers a credit card that can also be used in some 16,000 third-party retail outlets in northeastern Brazil.
Ahold said it and Bompreco planned considerable expansion in the north and northeast of Brazil in the coming years.
The Brazilian company currently operates seven so-called hypermarkets, 29 supermarkets, 11 minimarkets and three department stores that will be remodelled into hypermarkets.
